brief.summary: A household app where parents ask an AI to make illustrated bedtime stories for their children and keep every story they've ever generated in a shared family archive.
brief.user: Jonah Reyes, father of Pia (6) and Leo (9). He and his wife Hana both make stories, usually late at night and half-asleep, and they rarely name them well.
brief.moment: Pia's grandmother is visiting next weekend. Pia has asked for 'the dragon who was scared of the dark, the one with the lighthouse' so Grandma can read it to her, and Jonah wants to order a printed copy before Friday. He doesn't remember the title, whether he or Hana made it, or which of the several dragon stories it was. Some were made for Leo, and in some the dragon is scared of thunder instead. brief.data: 318 stories generated between May 2025 and November 2026: 204 made for Pia, 97 for Leo, 17 for both. Each story records its title (often auto-generated, like 'The Brave Little Glow'), who made it (Jonah 181, Hana 137), the date and time, the original prompt text, the target child and reading age, word count (300–1,400), the recurring characters used (e.g. Ember the dragon appears in 23 stories, Captain Biscuit the dog in 41), setting tags, number of illustrations (0–6), times read aloud, a heart if a child marked it a favorite, and any alternate versions or regenerated endings (52 stories have 2 or more versions). Nine stories mention both a dragon and a lighthouse. Three of those feature Ember being afraid of the dark, made March 3, March 4 and August 19, 2026, and the March 4 one has two endings. Printed-book orders so far: 4, the last in June 2026.

prompt:
I need the front end for Lanternloft. A household app where parents ask an AI to make illustrated bedtime stories for their children and keep every story they've ever generated in a shared family archive.

Who's using it: Jonah Reyes, father of Pia (6) and Leo (9). He and his wife Hana both make stories, usually late at night and half-asleep, and they rarely name them well.

What they're doing right now: Pia's grandmother is visiting next weekend. Pia has asked for 'the dragon who was scared of the dark, the one with the lighthouse' so Grandma can read it to her, and Jonah wants to order a printed copy before Friday. He doesn't remember the title, whether he or Hana made it, or which of the several dragon stories it was. Some were made for Leo, and in some the dragon is scared of thunder instead. He has to narrow hundreds of stories down to a few, compare them, and pick the right version. One story had a regenerated ending that Pia preferred.

What's in the system at this point: 318 stories generated between May 2025 and November 2026: 204 made for Pia, 97 for Leo, 17 for both. Each story records its title (often auto-generated, like 'The Brave Little Glow'), who made it (Jonah 181, Hana 137), the date and time, the original prompt text, the target child and reading age, word count (300–1,400), the recurring characters used (e.g. Ember the dragon appears in 23 stories, Captain Biscuit the dog in 41), setting tags, number of illustrations (0–6), times read aloud, a heart if a child marked it a favorite, and any alternate versions or regenerated endings (52 stories have 2 or more versions). Nine stories mention both a dragon and a lighthouse. Three of those feature Ember being afraid of the dark, made March 3, March 4 and August 19, 2026, and the March 4 one has two endings. Printed-book orders so far: 4, the last in June 2026.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
